Anathapindika.fact: Anathapindika (Pali: Anāthapiṇḍika; Sanskrit: Anāthapiṇḍada), born Sudatta, was a wealthy merchant, banker, and philanthropist, believed to have been the wealthiest merchant in Savatthi in the time of Gautama Buddha. Anathapindika.subject: Indian Architecture

He is considered to have been the chief male patron of the Buddha.

Anathapindika.subject: Indian Architecture
Anathapindika.question: He reached sotapanna, a stage of enlightenment, after listening to the _____ preach
Anathapindika.fact: Anathapindika was born into a wealthy merchant family in Savatthi with the birth name Sudatta, and was a relative of Subhūti, one of the Buddha's principal disciples. Anathapindika met the Buddha while on a business trip in Rājagaha after being told about him by his brother-in-law.

Anathapindika.subject: Indian Architecture
Anathapindika.question: He is known as the male lay disciple of the _____ who was foremost in generosity
Anathapindika.fact: After building Jetavana Monastery, Anathapindika continued to generously support the Buddha and his monastic community throughout his life and became called the Buddha's greatest patron and benefactor along with his female counterpart, Visakha. As chief patron, Anathapindika fed large numbers of the Buddha's monks daily and regularly maintained and supplied Jetavana Monastery, as well as served as one of the Buddha's primary aides in dealing with the general public.

Gautama Buddha's chief male patron was Anathapindika, with his chief female patron being Visakha.

Ashurbanipal.fact: Ashurbanipal (Neo-Assyrian Akkadian: 𒀸𒋩𒆕𒀀, romanized: Aššur-bāni-apli, meaning "Ashur is the creator of the heir") was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 669 BC to his death in 631. Ashurbanipal inherited the throne as his father Esarhaddon‘s favored heir; his 38-year reign was among the longest of any Assyrian king.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: He is generally remembered as the last great king of _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: Ashurbanipal (Neo-Assyrian Akkadian: 𒀸𒋩𒆕𒀀, romanized: Aššur-bāni-apli, meaning "Ashur is the creator of the heir") was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 669 BC to his death in 631. He is generally remembered as the last great king of Assyria.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Perhaps in order to avoid future rivalry, _____ designated Shamash-shum-ukin as the heir to Babylonia
Ashurbanipal.fact: Esarhaddon selected Ashurbanipal as heir c. Perhaps in order to avoid future rivalry, Esarhaddon designated Shamash-shum-ukin as the heir to Babylonia.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The more than 30,000 cuneiform texts that have survived from the library are a highly important source on ancient _____ language, religion, literature and science
Ashurbanipal.fact: The more than 30,000 cuneiform texts that have survived from the library are a highly important source on ancient Mesopotamian language, religion, literature and science.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: His extensive destruction of _____ has been described as a genocide
Ashurbanipal.fact: His extensive destruction of Elam has been described as a genocide.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: He also had an older sister, _____-eterat, and several younger brothers
Ashurbanipal.fact: He also had an older sister, Serua-eterat, and several younger brothers.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Scholars have speculated at _____'s reasons for the divided succession, which broke with the Assyrian tradition of unitary rule
Ashurbanipal.fact: Esarhaddon's own father Sennacherib had bypassed Esarhaddon's elder brother Arda-Mulissu for the crown, and the rejected heir had murdered Sennacherib, with Esarhaddon winning the ensuing civil war. After the death of his own heir, Esarhaddon quickly made new succession plans, naming his younger son Ashurbanipal as primary heir and emperor of Assyria, and his eldest surviving son Shamash-shum-ukin as king of Babylon (southern Mesopotamia), with the two to rule as "equal brothers".

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: However, it is equally likely that the two heirs shared a mother, possibly _____-hammat (Esarhaddon's primary consort)
Ashurbanipal.fact: However, it is equally likely that the two heirs shared a mother, possibly Esharra-hammat (Esarhaddon's primary consort).

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The two princes arrived at the _____ capital of Nineveh together and partook in a celebration in May 672 with foreign representatives, Assyrian nobles and military commanders
Ashurbanipal.fact: One hypothesis is that Ashurbanipal's mother was Assyrian while Shamash-shum-ukin's was Babylonian, which might have disfavored him for the Assyrian throne. The two princes arrived at the Assyrian capital of Nineveh together and partook in a celebration in May 672 with foreign representatives, Assyrian nobles and military commanders.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: He mounted to what may have been the most powerful throne on _____, but his sovereignty may not have been secure
Ashurbanipal.fact: He mounted to what may have been the most powerful throne on Earth, but his sovereignty may not have been secure.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Ashurbanipal inherited the throne as his father Esarhaddon‘s favored heir; his _____-year reign was among the longest of any Assyrian king
Ashurbanipal.fact: Ashurbanipal inherited the throne as his father Esarhaddon‘s favored heir; his 38-year reign was among the longest of any Assyrian king.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: It was _____'s greatest triumph and brought the Assyrian Empire to its greatest extent
Ashurbanipal.fact: Esarhaddon's succession decrees equivocated on the balance of power between the two heirs. It was Esarhaddon's greatest triumph and brought the Assyrian Empire to its greatest extent.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Assyrian control of Egypt was weak, however, as _____ retreated south to Nubia and schemed to retake his lands
Ashurbanipal.fact: Assyrian control of Egypt was weak, however, as Taharqa retreated south to Nubia and schemed to retake his lands. In 669, Taharqa led Egypt in a revolt against Assyria, and Esarhaddon left Nineveh to meet the threat, but fell ill and died on the way.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: In 669, _____ led Egypt in a revolt against Assyria, and Esarhaddon left Nineveh to meet the threat, but fell ill and died on the way
Ashurbanipal.fact: Assyrian control of Egypt was weak, however, as Taharqa retreated south to Nubia and schemed to retake his lands. In 669, Taharqa led Egypt in a revolt against Assyria, and Esarhaddon left Nineveh to meet the threat, but fell ill and died on the way.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Esarhaddon sent troops to garrison _____ cities and appointed local Egyptian nobles as vassal rulers of the country
Ashurbanipal.fact: Esarhaddon sent troops to garrison Egyptian cities and appointed local Egyptian nobles as vassal rulers of the country. The campaign lapsed while Ashurbanipal was succeeding to his father's throne, and many of the Egyptian vassal rulers joined the revolt to expel the foreign conquerors.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: On their way to Egypt, the _____ army collected tribute and military reinforcements from the various Levantine vassal states, including Manasseh of Judah and various rulers from Cyprus
Ashurbanipal.fact: After they massacred the Assyrian garrison in Memphis, Ashurbanipal sent an army against the rebels. On their way to Egypt, the Assyrian army collected tribute and military reinforcements from the various Levantine vassal states, including Manasseh of Judah and various rulers from Cyprus.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: According to _____ sources, Taharqa and his supporters fled from Memphis to Thebes, then escaped back to Nubia, and the Assyrian army re-occupied Memphis
Ashurbanipal.fact: After they massacred the Assyrian garrison in Memphis, Ashurbanipal sent an army against the rebels. On their way to Egypt, the Assyrian army collected tribute and military reinforcements from the various Levantine vassal states, including Manasseh of Judah and various rulers from Cyprus.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The expeditionary forces fought their way through Egypt, winning a decisive battle at Kar-Banitu in _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: The expeditionary forces fought their way through Egypt, winning a decisive battle at Kar-Banitu in Lower Egypt.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: In retaliation for the repeated rebellion, the _____ heavily plundered Thebes
Ashurbanipal.fact: In retaliation for the repeated rebellion, the Assyrians heavily plundered Thebes.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The sacking was the most serious calamity ever to befall the ancient city, one of the major political and religious centers in _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: By Ashurbanipal's account, Tantamani fled south as soon as the Assyrian army entered Egypt. The sacking was the most serious calamity ever to befall the ancient city, one of the major political and religious centers in Egypt.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The city might have been razed to the ground but for the skillful diplomacy of its governor _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: The city might have been razed to the ground but for the skillful diplomacy of its governor Mentuemhat.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Tantamani was not pursued beyond the _____ border
Ashurbanipal.fact: Tantamani was not pursued beyond the Egyptian border.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Urtak was successfully driven back into _____, dying shortly thereafter
Ashurbanipal.fact: Urtak was successfully driven back into Elam, dying shortly thereafter. He was succeeded as Elamite king by Teumman, who was unrelated to the previous monarch and had to stabilize his rule by killing his political rivals.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: He was succeeded as _____ king by Teumman, who was unrelated to the previous monarch and had to stabilize his rule by killing his political rivals
Ashurbanipal.fact: He was succeeded as Elamite king by Teumman, who was unrelated to the previous monarch and had to stabilize his rule by killing his political rivals. Three of Urtak's sons, chief rival claimants to the Elamite throne, escaped to Assyria and were harbored by Ashurbanipal, despite Teumman demanding them to be returned to Elam.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Bel-iqisha, chieftain of the _____ (an Aramean tribe) in Babylonia, rebelled after he had been implicated as supporting the Elamite invasion and was forced to relinquish some of his authority
Ashurbanipal.fact: Bel-iqisha, chieftain of the Gambulians (an Aramean tribe) in Babylonia, rebelled after he had been implicated as supporting the Elamite invasion and was forced to relinquish some of his authority.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Nabu-usabsi apparently claimed that Bel-iqisha was solely to blame for the _____ invasion
Ashurbanipal.fact: Following the 665 victory over the Elamites, Ashurbanipal had to deal with a series of revolts within his own borders. Bel-iqisha, chieftain of the Gambulians (an Aramean tribe) in Babylonia, rebelled after he had been implicated as supporting the Elamite invasion and was forced to relinquish some of his authority.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: After a long period of peace, _____ attacked Babylonia in 653
Ashurbanipal.fact: After a long period of peace, Teumman attacked Babylonia in 653. Though Teumman marched to meet the Assyrians, he soon changed his mind and fell back to the Elamite capital of Susa.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Though Teumman marched to meet the _____, he soon changed his mind and fell back to the Elamite capital of Susa
Ashurbanipal.fact: Though Teumman marched to meet the Assyrians, he soon changed his mind and fell back to the Elamite capital of Susa.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The final battle in the war with _____, the Battle of Ulai, took place near Susa and was a decisive Assyrian victory, partly due to defections in the Elamite army
Ashurbanipal.fact: Though Teumman marched to meet the Assyrians, he soon changed his mind and fell back to the Elamite capital of Susa. The final battle in the war with Teumman, the Battle of Ulai, took place near Susa and was a decisive Assyrian victory, partly due to defections in the Elamite army.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Teumann was killed in the battle, as was one of his vassals, _____-Nahhunte of Hidalu
Ashurbanipal.fact: Teumann was killed in the battle, as was one of his vassals, Shutruk-Nahhunte of Hidalu.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: This intervention into the _____ succession weakened both Elamite opposition towards Assyria and Elamite royal authority
Ashurbanipal.fact: The final battle in the war with Teumman, the Battle of Ulai, took place near Susa and was a decisive Assyrian victory, partly due to defections in the Elamite army. This intervention into the Elamite succession weakened both Elamite opposition towards Assyria and Elamite royal authority.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: I cut off the head of _____, their king, – the haughty one, who plotted evil
Ashurbanipal.fact: I cut off the head of Teumann, their king, – the haughty one, who plotted evil.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: With their corpses I filled the plain about _____ as with baltu and ashagu
Ashurbanipal.fact: With their corpses I filled the plain about Susa as with baltu and ashagu.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Their blood I let run down the _____; its water I dyed red like wool
Ashurbanipal.fact: Their blood I let run down the Ulai; its water I dyed red like wool.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Dunanu, who had joined the _____ in the war, was captured alongside his family and executed
Ashurbanipal.fact: Dunanu, who had joined the Elamites in the war, was captured alongside his family and executed.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: After Esarhaddon defeated them, the _____ turned to attack Lydia in western Anatolia, ruled by Gyges
Ashurbanipal.fact: After Esarhaddon defeated them, the Cimmerians turned to attack Lydia in western Anatolia, ruled by Gyges.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The Assyrians did not even know that Lydia existed; after the two states successfully established communication with the help of interpreters, the _____ invasion of Lydia was defeated c
Ashurbanipal.fact: After Esarhaddon defeated them, the Cimmerians turned to attack Lydia in western Anatolia, ruled by Gyges. The Assyrians did not even know that Lydia existed; after the two states successfully set up communication with the help of interpreters, the Cimmerian invasion of Lydia was defeated c.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: 652–650 there was much rejoicing in _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: The extent to which the Assyrian army was involved in the Lydian campaign is unknown, but it appears that Gyges was disappointed with the help since he just twelve years later broke his alliance with Ashurbanipal and allied with the increasingly independent Egypt instead. 652–650 there was much rejoicing in Assyria.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: While the _____ forces were on campaign in Elam, an alliance of Persians, Cimmerians and Medes marched on Nineveh and managed to reach the city's walls
Ashurbanipal.fact: While the Assyrian forces were on campaign in Elam, an alliance of Persians, Cimmerians and Medes marched on Nineveh and managed to reach the city's walls. To counteract this threat, Ashurbanipal called on Assyria´s longtime ally, the Indo-Aryan (Iranic) Scythian allies, and the Assyrians and Scythians successfully defeated the enemy army.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The Median king, _____, is generally held to have been killed in the fighting
Ashurbanipal.fact: The Median king, Phraortes, is generally held to have been killed in the fighting. This attack is poorly documented and it is possible that Phraortes was not present at all and his unfortunate death instead belongs to a Median campaign during the reign of one of Ashurbanipal's successors.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: 652, _____ was succeeded by his son Ardys
Ashurbanipal.fact: 652, Gyges was succeeded by his son Ardys.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Because the _____ had driven the Cimmerians from their homes, the Cimmerians invaded Lydia again and successfully captured of the kingdom
Ashurbanipal.fact: Because the Scythians had driven the Cimmerians from their homes, the Cimmerians invaded Lydia again and successfully captured of the kingdom.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: It is unknown if any _____ aid arrived, but Lydia was successfully freed from the Cimmerians
Ashurbanipal.fact: It is unknown if any Assyrian aid arrived, but Lydia was successfully freed from the Cimmerians.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: They would not be driven out of Lydia completely until the reign of Ardys's grandson _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: They would not be driven out of Lydia completely until the reign of Ardys's grandson Alyattes.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Despite this, _____-shum-ukin had initially been positively inclined towards his brother, viewing him as his equal
Ashurbanipal.fact: Despite this, Shamash-shum-ukin had initially been positively inclined towards his brother, viewing him as his equal. In letters, Shamash-shum-ukin addressed Ashurbanipal simply as "my brother" (unlike how he addressed his father Esarhaddon, "the king, my father").

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Zakir reported that though _____-shum-ukin was angered, he and his governor of Babylon, Ubaru, chose to not take action against the visitors
Ashurbanipal.fact: By the 650s, Shamash-shum-ukin's opinion of Ashurbanipal had significantly deteriorated, owing to the increasing intervention and involvement of Ashurbanipal in Babylonian affairs, Ashurbanipal often delaying when help was needed, and growing dissatisfaction with his position relative to that of Ashurbanipal. A letter written during this time by Zakir, a courtier at Shamash-shum-ukin's court, to Ashurbanipal described how visitors from the Sea Land had publicly criticized Ashurbanipal in fron...

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Inscription evidence suggests that _____-shum-ukin addressed the citizens of Babylon to join him in his revolt
Ashurbanipal.fact: According to later Aramaic-language legends, Ashurbanipal's and Shamash-shum-ukin's sister Serua-eterat attempted to intervene and stop the two from fighting; after the war broke out the legends hold that she disappeared into self-imposed exile. In addition to resenting Ashurbanipal's overbearing control, Shamash-shum-ukin's revolt was also facilitated by the certainty of support in the south: the Babylonians constantly resented Assyrian control and the rulers of Elam were certain allies, alw...

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The Babylonians, who had been loyal to _____ and faithful vassals of mine, he deceived, speaking lies to them
Ashurbanipal.fact: The Babylonians, who had been loyal to Assyria and faithful vassals of mine, he deceived, speaking lies to them.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: It has been theorized by scholars that "_____" refers to the Medes (as Gutium no longer existed at this point) but this is uncertain
Ashurbanipal.fact: Ashurbanipal identified three groups who aided his brother: first and foremost there were the Chaldeans, Arameans and the other peoples of Babylonia, then there were the Elamites, and lastly the kings of Gutium, Amurru and Meluhha. It has been theorized by scholars that "Gutium" refers to the Medes (as Gutium no longer existed at this point) but this is uncertain.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Meluhha might have referred to Egypt, though the _____ are not documented for certain to have aided Shamash-shum-ukin in the war
Ashurbanipal.fact: Meluhha might have referred to Egypt, though the Egyptians are not documented for certain to have aided Shamash-shum-ukin in the war.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: For the first two years of the conflict, battles were fought all across _____, some won by the Assyrians and some won by Shamash-shum-ukin and his allies
Ashurbanipal.fact: For the first two years of the conflict, battles were fought all across Babylonia, some won by the Assyrians and some won by Shamash-shum-ukin and his allies. Among the most notorious double agents were Nabu-bel-shumati, a governor of the far south in Babylonia whose repeated betrayals enraged Ashurbanipal.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Having endured both starvation and disease, _____ fell in 648, after a siege lasting two years
Ashurbanipal.fact: By 650 the situation looked grim, with Ashurbanipal's forces having besieged Sippar, Borsippa, Kutha and Babylon itself. During Ashurbanipal's siege of Babylon, the city entered into a period of famine.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: At the time of the city's fall, a great fire also spread within _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: Having endured both starvation and disease, Babylon fell in 648, after a siege lasting two years. At the time of the city's fall, a great fire also spread within Babylon.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The authority of _____ is likely to have been very limited and few records survive of his reign at Babylon
Ashurbanipal.fact: After Shamash-shum-ukin's defeat, Ashurbanipal appointed a new vassal king of Babylon, Kandalanu, of whom little is known. Kandalanu's realm was the same as Shamash-shum-ukin's with the exception of the city of Nippur, which Ashurbanipal converted into a powerful Assyrian fortress.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The civil war also had significant broader consequences impacting _____ dominion
Ashurbanipal.fact: Due to the defeat and death of a member of the Assyrian royal family, the defeat of Shamash-shum-ukin was Ashurbanipal's most problematic victory. The civil war also had significant broader consequences impacting Assyrian dominion.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Signs of decline had already been visible before the civil war but its conclusion is regarded by modern historians to mark the end of the height of _____ authority
Ashurbanipal.fact: Due to the defeat and death of a member of the Assyrian royal family, the defeat of Shamash-shum-ukin was Ashurbanipal's most problematic victory. The civil war also had significant broader consequences impacting Assyrian dominion.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Though Babylonia slowly recovered after the war, the war exhausted economic resources and decreased the power and authority of the _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: Though Babylonia slowly recovered after the war, the war exhausted economic resources and decreased the power and authority of the Assyrian Empire.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: As a result of _____'s defeat, he was deposed in Elam by Tammaritu II, who then took the throne for himself
Ashurbanipal.fact: As a result of Ummanigash's defeat, he was deposed in Elam by Tammaritu II, who then took the throne for himself. Ummanigash fled to the Assyrian court where he was granted asylum by Ashurbanipal.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: After the _____ defense collapsed, Humban-haltash abandoned his seat at Madaktu and fled into the mountains
Ashurbanipal.fact: After the Elamite defense collapsed, Humban-haltash abandoned his seat at Madaktu and fled into the mountains.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: He was briefly replaced as king by _____, who regained his throne
Ashurbanipal.fact: He was briefly replaced as king by Tammaritu II, who regained his throne.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: After the _____ had plundered the region of Khuzestan they returned home, prompting Humban-haltash to reemerge from the mountains and retake the throne
Ashurbanipal.fact: Because Humban-haltash could thus not respond to Ashurbanipal's threats, the Assyrians invaded Elam again in 647. After the Assyrians had plundered the region of Khuzestan they returned home, prompting Humban-haltash to reemerge from the mountains and retake the throne.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: The Assyrians returned to Elam in _____ and Humban-haltash again abandoned Madaktu, fleeing first to the city Dur-Untash and then into the mountains in eastern Elam
Ashurbanipal.fact: The Assyrians returned to Elam in 646 and Humban-haltash again abandoned Madaktu, fleeing first to the city Dur-Untash and then into the mountains in eastern Elam.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Among these kingdoms was _____, possibly a predecessor of the empire that would be founded by the Achaemenids a century later
Ashurbanipal.fact: Among these kingdoms was Parsua, possibly a predecessor of the empire that would be set up by the Achaemenids a century later. Parsua's king, Cyrus (possibly the same person as Cyrus I, the grandfather of Cyrus the Great), had originally sided with the Elamites at the beginning of the campaign, and had thus been forced to supply his son Arukku as a hostage.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: On their way back from their campaign, the _____ forces brutally plundered Susa
Ashurbanipal.fact: Countries which had never previously had contact with the Assyrians, such as a kingdom ruled by a king called Ḫudimiri which "extended beyond Elam", also began paying tribute to the Assyrians for the first time. On their way back from their campaign, the Assyrian forces brutally plundered Susa.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: In addition to the destruction of numerous cities, thousands of those _____ who were not killed were deported away from their homeland
Ashurbanipal.fact: In addition to the destruction of numerous cities, thousands of those Elamites who were not killed were deported away from their homeland. The detail and length of Ashurbanipal's inscriptions concerning the destructions suggest that the events were meant to shock the world, signalling the defeat and eradication of the Elamites as a distinct cultural entity.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Susa, the great holy city, abode of their gods, seat of their mysteries, I conquered according to the word of Ashur and _____
Ashurbanipal.fact: Susa, the great holy city, abode of their gods, seat of their mysteries, I conquered according to the word of Ashur and Ishtar.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: I destroyed the ziggurat of _____ [...]; I smashed its shining copper horns
Ashurbanipal.fact: Susa, the great holy city, abode of their gods, seat of their mysteries, I conquered according to the word of Ashur and Ishtar. I destroyed the ziggurat of Susa [...]; I smashed its shining copper horns.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: I reduced the temples of _____ to naught; their gods, their goddesses, I scattered to the winds
Ashurbanipal.fact: I entered its palaces, I dwelt there in rejoicing; I opened the treasures where silver and gold, goods and wealth were amassed [...] the treasures of Sumer, Akkad, and Babylon that the ancient kings of Elam had looted and carried away [...]. I reduced the temples of Elam to naught; their gods, their goddesses, I scattered to the winds.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: [...] I devastated the provinces of _____ and [on their lands] I spread salt [...]
Ashurbanipal.fact: I reduced the temples of Elam to naught; their gods, their goddesses, I scattered to the winds. [...] I devastated the provinces of Elam and [on their lands] I spread salt [...].

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Despite the thorough and brutal campaign, the _____ endured as a political entity for some time
Ashurbanipal.fact: Despite the thorough and brutal campaign, the Elamites endured as a political entity for some time.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: On occasion, the _____ army intervened, deposing and replacing problematic tribal rulers
Ashurbanipal.fact: After Humban-haltash was deposed, captured and sent to the Assyrians in a revolt shortly thereafter, Assyrian records cease to speak of Elam. On occasion, the Assyrian army intervened, deposing and replacing problematic tribal rulers.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Ammuladdin was captured and sent in chains to _____ but Yauta escaped
Ashurbanipal.fact: Ashurbanipal's earliest account of his campaign against the Qedarites was created in 649 BC and describes how Yauta, son of Ḫazaʾil, king of the Qedarites, revolted against Ashurbanipal together with another Arab king, Ammuladdin, and plundered the western lands of the Assyrian Empire. According to Ashurbanipal's account, the Assyrian army, together with the army of Kamas-halta of Moab, defeated the rebel forces.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: In the place of Yauta a loyal _____ warlord called Abiyate was granted kingship of the Qedarites
Ashurbanipal.fact: In the place of Yauta a loyal Arabian warlord called Abiyate was granted kingship of the Qedarites.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Even later versions of the narrative also include mentions of how Yauta previously revolted against _____, years prior
Ashurbanipal.fact: Even later versions of the narrative also include mentions of how Yauta previously revolted against Esarhaddon, years prior.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: In both accounts, the _____ lands were thoroughly plundered at the conclusion of the war
Ashurbanipal.fact: In both accounts, the Qedarite lands were thoroughly plundered at the conclusion of the war.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Some of the Arab tribal leaders joined _____-shum-ukin in the Assyrian civil war
Ashurbanipal.fact: These later accounts also explicitly connect Yauta's rebellion to the revolt of Shamash-shum-ukin, placing it at the same time and suggesting that the western raids by the Arabs were prompted by the instability caused by the Assyrian civil war. Some of the Arab tribal leaders joined Shamash-shum-ukin in the Assyrian civil war.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: According to the account, the _____ army marched from Syria to Damascus and then on to Hulhuliti, after which they captured Abiyate and defeated Uššo and Akko
Ashurbanipal.fact: As the Elamite wars dragged on, several Arab rulers ceased to pay tribute to Ashurbanipal and began raiding nearby Assyrian settlements, severely disrupting trade. According to the account, the Assyrian army marched from Syria to Damascus and then on to Hulhuliti, after which they captured Abiyate and defeated Uššo and Akko.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: In this version, _____ and Ammuladdin are specified to have joined Shamash-shum-ukin
Ashurbanipal.fact: In this version, Abiyate and Ammuladdin are specified to have joined Shamash-shum-ukin.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
Ashurbanipal.question: Supposedly spoils brought back from the _____ campaigns were so extensive that they caused inflation in the Assyrian Empire and famine in Arabia
Ashurbanipal.fact: Supposedly spoils brought back from the Arabian campaigns were so extensive that they caused inflation in the Assyrian Empire and famine in Arabia. Despite this, and despite being impressive in the sense that no previous Assyrian ruler had campaigned against the Arabs with the same vigor, Ashurbanipal's Arabian campaigns are sometimes assessed as a strategic blunder.

Ashurbanipal.subject: Indian Architecture
